title: Competitors
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-customers-suppliers-competitors, covers customers, suppliers and competitors together, so it is broader than the new point, which is about competitors alone.

draft.title: Competitors
card: Competitors are other businesses that sell similar products to the same customers. A new business must plan with them in mind.
A new business looks at what competitors charge, what they sell and how they promote. This helps it set its own prices and choose its range.
It can also look for a gap, such as a product or service that competitors do not offer well, and plan to fill it.
Competitors keep acting after the new business opens. They may cut prices or add products, so the plans may need to change.
draft.remember: Know what competitors charge, sell and might do next, then plan to stand out.

a.q: Why does a new business study the prices and products of its competitors?
opts: To help it plan prices and products that stand out
To copy every price and product that they offer
To prove that no changes will be needed later
To make sure that customers have no other choices
a.why: Studying competitors helps the business set prices and choose products that give customers a reason to pick it. It does not need to copy them, and it cannot remove customers' other choices.
a.clue: Think about how the information helps its own plan.

b.q: Tom plans a bike repair shop in Geelong. Two nearby shops repair bikes, but neither offers pick-up. What is the best use of this information?
opts: Plan a pick-up service to fill the gap in the market
Charge less than both shops to attract more customers
Open without a plan, as the two shops do the same job
Drop the plan, as repair shops already exist nearby
b.why: Competitors do not offer pick-up, so this is a gap Tom can plan to fill. Charging less is possible, but it ignores the gap, and the existing shops do not mean there is no room.
b.clue: Look at what the competitors do not offer.

a.best: To help it plan prices and products that stand out

b.best: Plan a pick-up service to fill the gap in the market
